### workspace launch --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace launch [options] <project1> [project2] ...

Launch tmuxinator projects in iTerm2, each in its own window.
Reuses existing launcher panes when available.
Windows are arranged left-to-right with slight overlap.

Options:
        --reattach                   Reuse a launcher pane's existing tmux session instead of relaunching
                                     into it (see docs/README.launch.md).
        --[no-]headless              Start each session in the background with plain tmux: no iTerm2,
                                     AppleScript or window-tool. Default: the launch.headless config key if set,
                                     else headless when not on macOS, when osascript is missing, or when CI is set
        --prompt PROMPT              Send an initial prompt to the coding agent in each project, once it is
                                     ready (up to 60s); exits 1 if it can't be sent
        --prompt-timeout DURATION    How long to wait for the coding agent to be ready for --prompt
                                     (e.g. "90s", or a plain number of seconds); default 60s
        --play NAME[,NAME...]        Send each project's agent 'Read "<path>" and follow it.' for a library play,
                                     then any --prompt text. Repeatable, and each value may list plays separated by
                                     commas; the agent gets one line per play, in order. Looked up per project (its
                                     library, then global); an unknown or unreadable play fails before anything launches
        --pack NAME                  Also send the agent a library pack's text with the first prompt (repeatable; see
                                     'workspace instructions compose --help'). An unknown pack fails before anything launches
        --no-packs                   Send no automatic packs (the notes pack, unless notes.instructions is false;
                                     the spine pack, when spine/ exists; the dev pack, when dev.up is set; the handoff pack, when handoff.auto is true);
                                     cannot be combined with --pack
        --[no-]handoff               Send (or never send) the handoff pack, whatever handoff.auto says. It makes a Claude
                                     Code or Codex agent run 'workspace handoff check' after every task. --handoff for a project
                                     whose main agent is neither fails before anything launches (handoff_unsupported_agent)
        --arrange                    Tile the new windows, ignoring the window positions saved when they were
                                     stopped (launch.restore_window_position false does the same on every launch)
        --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md) instead of progress text;
                                     the text goes to stderr. Exit 0, 3 when some projects failed, 1 when all did

Headless: a session already running is reused as it is; attach with
'tmux attach -t <session>'. --reattach has no effect headless.

Note: --reattach uses tmux -CC attach which may trigger an iTerm dialog.
To suppress it, set iTerm > Settings > General > tmux >
  'When attaching, restore windows' to 'Always'.

A directory path creates a config named in lowercase. A name that differs only
in case from another workspace's is refused (workspace_name_case_conflict); the
same directory's mixed-case config is reused.

Examples:
  workspace launch my-project    # launch one project by name
  workspace launch my-notes work-notes billing    # launch several projects
  workspace launch ~/Code/my-project    # launch from a directory path (creates a config)
  workspace launch --reattach my-project    # reuse the pane's existing tmux session
  workspace launch --arrange my-project    # tile the window, ignoring its saved position
  workspace launch --prompt "Review the README" my-project    # send the agent an initial prompt
  workspace launch --play kickoff my-project    # point the agent at a library play
  workspace launch --play kickoff,review my-project    # two plays; --play a --play b does the same
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace launch
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
Usage: workspace launch [options] <project1> [project2] ...

Launch tmuxinator projects in iTerm2, each in its own window.
Reuses existing launcher panes when available.
Windows are arranged left-to-right with slight overlap.

Options:
        --reattach                   Reuse a launcher pane's existing tmux session instead of relaunching
                                     into it (see docs/README.launch.md).
        --[no-]headless              Start each session in the background with plain tmux: no iTerm2,
                                     AppleScript or window-tool. Default: the launch.headless config key if set,
                                     else headless when not on macOS, when osascript is missing, or when CI is set
        --prompt PROMPT              Send an initial prompt to the coding agent in each project, once it is
                                     ready (up to 60s); exits 1 if it can't be sent
        --prompt-timeout DURATION    How long to wait for the coding agent to be ready for --prompt
                                     (e.g. "90s", or a plain number of seconds); default 60s
        --play NAME[,NAME...]        Send each project's agent 'Read "<path>" and follow it.' for a library play,
                                     then any --prompt text. Repeatable, and each value may list plays separated by
                                     commas; the agent gets one line per play, in order. Looked up per project (its
                                     library, then global); an unknown or unreadable play fails before anything launches
        --pack NAME                  Also send the agent a library pack's text with the first prompt (repeatable; see
                                     'workspace instructions compose --help'). An unknown pack fails before anything launches
        --no-packs                   Send no automatic packs (the notes pack, unless notes.instructions is false;
                                     the spine pack, when spine/ exists; the dev pack, when dev.up is set; the handoff pack, when handoff.auto is true);
                                     cannot be combined with --pack
        --[no-]handoff               Send (or never send) the handoff pack, whatever handoff.auto says. It makes a Claude
                                     Code or Codex agent run 'workspace handoff check' after every task. --handoff for a project
                                     whose main agent is neither fails before anything launches (handoff_unsupported_agent)
        --arrange                    Tile the new windows, ignoring the window positions saved when they were
                                     stopped (launch.restore_window_position false does the same on every launch)
        --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md) instead of progress text;
                                     the text goes to stderr. Exit 0, 3 when some projects failed, 1 when all did

Headless: a session already running is reused as it is; attach with
'tmux attach -t <session>'. --reattach has no effect headless.

Note: --reattach uses tmux -CC attach which may trigger an iTerm dialog.
To suppress it, set iTerm > Settings > General > tmux >
  'When attaching, restore windows' to 'Always'.

A directory path creates a config named in lowercase. A name that differs only
in case from another workspace's is refused (workspace_name_case_conflict); the
same directory's mixed-case config is reused.

Examples:
  workspace launch my-project    # launch one project by name
  workspace launch my-notes work-notes billing    # launch several projects
  workspace launch ~/Code/my-project    # launch from a directory path (creates a config)
  workspace launch --reattach my-project    # reuse the pane's existing tmux session

  workspace launch --prompt "Review the README" my-project    # send the agent an initial prompt
  workspace launch --play kickoff my-project    # point the agent at a library play
  workspace launch --play kickoff,review my-project    # two plays; --play a --play b does the same
